posts.title: Reverse engineering a vintage diode-transistor logic chip
posts.description: Going through a collection of old parts, CuriousMarc encountered some ICs that he couldn't identify. He opened up one of these ICs, and I studied it under the microscope. posts.title: Inside the Intel 8087 chip: floating-point addition and subtraction
posts.description: In 1980, Intel introduced the 8087, a chip that made floating-point operations much faster in the IBM PC and other systems. Although the 8087 supports advanced operations such as tangents, square roots, and logarithms, this article focuses on basic arithmetic operations: addition and subtraction.
